455.skill_name: Assess Workplace Interaction and Work Functioning
455.skill_description: Inquire about the quality of interaction and communication patterns with supervisors/colleagues, record tense, conflict, and impatience responses, as well as avoidance strategies and consequences such as avoiding eye contact, avoiding actions in front of others, or choosing smaller group times, assess efficiency and role impairment.
455.when_to_use: When assessing social life and work functioning, when workplace difficulties are prominent or when shifting to the work dimension.
455.trigger: Client mentions increased criticism, communication obstruction, decreased work efficiency, or avoidance of necessary social interaction.

330.skill_name: Assess Learning Efficiency and Attention Changes
330.skill_description: Specifically inquire about learning attitude, attention and classroom participation, homework completion and attendance, and compare recent efficiency and grade changes, delineate the scope and time correspondence of academic functioning impairment.
330.when_to_use: When assessing academic role functioning and daily task completion, or when quantifying impairment and recovery.
330.trigger: Client or parent mentions zoning out in class, decreased learning efficiency, procrastination, or still attending class but low efficiency.

264.skill_name: Verify and Record Core Demographics and Educational Information
264.skill_description: Based on registration forms and interviews, verify and record core information such as age, gender, ethnicity, grade level/educational stage and major, origin/place of birth, and can supplement observable data such as current status, height/weight/build, and appearance to form a clear and comparable background baseline, supporting subsequent assessment and communication.
264.when_to_use: At the beginning of data collection for initial consultation or assessment sessions 1-2, when establishing the client's background profile.
264.trigger: First visit or incomplete/vague registration data, requiring completion of basic information such as age, gender, grade, major, origin.

359.skill_name: Collect and verify demographic items using the record form
359.skill_description: Guide the completion and on-site verification of consultation/registration forms, systemically record basic information such as age, gender, educational level/grade, origin, and place of residence, supplement family composition when necessary, ensure data accuracy, completeness, and traceability, provide background support for subsequent assessments.
359.when_to_use: During the initial contact or first interview, used to establish basic data and assessment framework.
359.trigger: Start filling out the record form during the first visit, or when existing data is missing/unclear and system verification is required.

441.skill_name: Inquire and record family structure and living/growth background
441.skill_description: Briefly inquire and record information regarding whether single-parent, cohabiting members, family composition and relationship status, living arrangements, and growth environment and ranking, clarify the relationship with the care recipient and main identity when necessary, as basic data for social support and family background.
441.when_to_use: During the basic information collection phase of the initial interview, supplement demographic data with family and living/growth background.
441.trigger: When the visitor mentions family or living/growth clues, or when family composition and relationship status are not yet specified.

239.skill_name: Record family composition, parental occupation, and economic status
239.skill_description: Ask and record information such as the number of people in the family, parents' occupations and economic status, parental relationship/separation, number of siblings and relationship with them, to form a profile of family resources and pressures, as a basis for social support assessment and conceptualization.
239.when_to_use: During the assessment phase when collecting basic information and social background, or before case conceptualization.
239.trigger: When discussing 'family situation' but information is incomplete, or when needing to understand family members and parents' occupations and economic status.

249.skill_name: Collect education, occupation, and living information
249.skill_description: Inquire and record the highest education level, current job position, work city, and whether they live in the same city as family members, supplement marital and child information when necessary, to grasp social support, role pressure, and resource accessibility.
249.when_to_use: During the initial interview or the first phase of data collection, used to complete basic case information.
249.trigger: When the visitor mentions graduation and work, living in a different city, or information about spouse/children is unclear.

514.skill_name: Collect and verify basic identity and educational information
514.skill_description: Through registration forms and interviews in the initial visit, clarify and record core identity information such as age, gender, ethnicity, place of origin/residence, grade level/educational stage, and can supplement height and physical appearance and reasons for consultation, forming a complete background file and baseline for comparison.
514.when_to_use: During the first to second assessment/case establishment phase, when establishing the case's basic situation and background.
514.trigger: First visit or when basic information such as age, gender, grade level, etc., needs to be completed when records are missing/incomplete.

398.skill_name: Use interview/registration form system to collect general demographic data
398.skill_description: Have the visitor fill out the interview/registration form and verify, the system records basic information such as age, gender, ethnicity, grade level, and when necessary, supplementary information on living situation and social support items, ensuring the data is complete, accurate, and traceable, providing background for assessment and diagnosis.
398.when_to_use: When collecting data during the initial consultation's assessment and relationship building phase.
398.trigger: When the initial visit has not provided basic information or when a complete case file needs to be established.

205.skill_name: Record personal and family information through interview and forms
205.skill_description: Based on the case overview and registration form, comprehensively record personal information such as age, gender, grade level, height/physique/year of birth through communication and questioning, as well as family composition, economic status, and parental relationships/occupation, forming complete background data for subsequent assessment.
205.when_to_use: During the initial stage of collecting interview data or writing the case overview.
205.trigger: When the visitor/family provides basic and family situations, or when registration data needs to be completed and verified.

164.skill_name: Clarify current grade level and recent wishes/goals
164.skill_description: When collecting educational information, inquire about and record the current grade level and recent wishes/goals (such as getting into an ideal university), to understand the context and motivation of the issue, and to provide clues for subsequent goal setting.
164.when_to_use: During the initial assessment phase for demographic and background information collection, or when assessing learning-related difficulties.
164.trigger: When the visitor is a student, or when they proactively mention learning goals and aspirations for further study.

299.skill_name: Collect and Record Core Demographics and Academic Information
299.skill_description: Systematically inquire and record basic information such as age, gender, ethnicity, marital/relationship status, educational level, residence, and current academic performance during intake interviews, forming case files necessary for subsequent assessment and background description.
299.when_to_use: During the intake interview phase of the initial consultation, used to establish the client's file and background.
299.trigger: When the client does not proactively provide information such as age, educational level, residence, or academic performance.

293.skill_name: Use Registration Form to Structure Collect and Verify Basic Information
293.skill_description: Systematically inquire and record basic information such as age, gender, origin, grade level, family composition, and economic status according to the registration form, and verify with the client's self-report on the spot to ensure background information is complete and consistent, and reliable.
293.when_to_use: During the initial consultation, used to establish the case file and background profile.
293.trigger: When there is no registration file or past information is incomplete and needs systematic supplementation.

265.skill_name: Outline Family Structure, Parental Occupation, and Economic Status
265.skill_description: Understand and record whether the client is single/only child/sibling, cohabiting members, family composition, parents' occupations and education, family economic status, and actual companionship/support levels, verify family psychiatric history when necessary, to present the background framework of social support and real-life stress.
265.when_to_use: When collecting basic information, supplement family and social support background for comprehensive assessment.
265.trigger: When the client mentions parents, cohabitation/economic situation, or single child background, or when related information is not recorded in the file.

364.skill_name: Collect Identity and Education Information via Intake Interview and Registration Form
364.skill_description: During the intake interview and registration form process, systematically record gender, year of birth, ethnicity, grade level/repetition experience, and institution for identity and educational background information, supplement origin, marital/religious status items when necessary, to provide references for subsequent assessment and intervention.
364.when_to_use: For collecting intake interview materials during the initial consultation, used to establish the basic case file and background.
364.trigger: When the initial visit or file is missing, and basic identity and educational information have not been recorded or are incomplete.

498.skill_name: Use registration form or verbal inquiry to collect demographic information
498.skill_description: Systematically collect demographic information such as gender, age, ethnicity, grade level; if the visitor is unwilling to fill out the form, use verbal inquiry and record it to ensure the basic file is complete and usable.
498.when_to_use: During the relationship building and assessment phase at the first interview.
498.trigger: First help-seeking and information not systematically recorded, or when the visitor refuses/has not filled out the registration form.

428.skill_name: Record academic performance and social roles
428.skill_description: Record academic grades, in-school positions and honors (such as party member, student cadre, scholarship, etc.), and interpersonal overview, depicting current identity and workload, as background data for social support and functioning assessment.
428.when_to_use: When establishing a basic file and needing to assess social support and functional background.
428.trigger: When the visitor mentions studies, grades, interpersonal relationships, or positions/honors experiences.

431.skill_description: Clarify and record the current grade level, whether living in residence/with whom, living independently, and dormitory/room life; academic and living information serves as the basis for environmental background and campus resource assessment.
431.when_to_use: In the basic information collection stage, used to supplement learning and living environment information.
431.trigger: When the visitor mentions in-school studies, accommodation arrangements, or needs to assess campus resources and support systems.

136.skill_name: Verify family structure and guardianship/single child information
136.skill_description: When collecting basic information, inquire about and record family composition, whether a single child, and guardianship/care arrangements, as background for subsequent family relationship assessment and conceptualization of social support.
136.when_to_use: When initial assessment collects general information and needs to understand family background and guardianship situation.
136.trigger: When the visitor mentions family, guardianship, or has not explained family structure and single child status.

307.skill_name: Inquire about family psychological and family illness background
307.skill_description: Supplemently verify whether parents have personality or neurotic disorders, understand if there is a history of mental illness in the family, and record it in basic information for comprehensive judgment of risk and resources.
307.when_to_use: Supplement family background and risk assessment during the initial assessment to complete basic data.
307.trigger: When the psychological health situation of parents and family is unclear or not recorded.

198.skill_name: Obtain information on residence and primary caregiver/nurturer
198.skill_description: Organize changes in past and current living arrangements and primary caregivers/nurturers (such as living with grandparents or parents), record who the person communicates with most often, in order to assess the living environment and support system.
198.when_to_use: During the initial conversation or background collection, organize the aspects of living environment and upbringing background.
198.trigger: When the client mentions their growth experience or is asked about past/current living and care arrangements.

376.skill_name: Confirm duration of care responsibility and daily arrangements
376.skill_description: When the client is the primary caregiver, inquire about the start time, duration, and daily care arrangements of becoming a caregiver, and understand whether they can leave the cared-for person and ways of supporting the children, to present the baseline of the care situation.
376.when_to_use: After collecting background information, transition to the care situation organization and support assessment stage.
376.trigger: When the client mentions taking on the primary care responsibility or describes the cared-for person's constraints.

128.skill_name: Observe and record first impression and motivation for seeking help
128.skill_description: During the initial entry and opening conversation, observe and record appearance, demeanor, verbal characteristics, logical clarity, emotional expression, and politeness, and inquire and confirm the desire/motivation for seeking help and sense of trust, as a reference for functional status and cooperation level.
128.when_to_use: In the first meeting and the beginning of the conversation, in the early stage before sufficient conversation.
128.trigger: Obvious clues such as clothing and posture upon entry, speech rate and logic, active seeking of help, or expression of trust.

360.skill_name: Observe and Record Appearance and Current Emotion/Behavior
360.skill_description: Begin recording observable appearance and behavioral states during the session, such as hairstyle, clothing, facial expression and posture, crying and reactions after soothing, fluency of language, etc., objectively describing basic information and current adaptation status.
360.when_to_use: Used during initial visits or the first day of hospitalization to establish a baseline performance.
360.trigger: When significant physical features or immediate emotional/behavioral reactions (such as crying, tense posture) are available for observation.

470.skill_name: Introduce and Set Up Thought Record
470.skill_description: Explain the structure and purpose of the thought/emotion record tool to the visitor, record triggering situations, automatic thoughts, emotion intensity, and behavioral reactions in daily situations, and attempt to write rational responses or supporting/opposing evidence. Demonstrate and practice in the session, as a basis for self-monitoring and preliminary testing of automatic thoughts during the session.
470.when_to_use: In the early to second stages of consultation, when beginning to identify automatic thoughts, needing structured organization of emotion-thought-behavior relationships, or entering the behavior training and homework phase.
470.trigger: When the visitor experiences negative emotions such as anxiety or sadness in typical situations or automatic thoughts; when narratives are scattered and difficult to grasp patterns; when peer/sibling conflict or interpersonal conflict is frequent and needs structured recording.

335.skill_name: Clarify Recording Timing and Provide Continuous Feedback
335.skill_description: Agree on recording rules with the visitor: immediately record the event, thoughts, and emotions when noticing a change in mood or worsening; continuously record emotional and behavioral changes and reactions in daily life. Bring back feedback from homework regularly, the therapist checks and adjusts the practice if necessary, to strengthen self-awareness, self-assessment, and self-guidance, consolidating new concepts and strategies.
335.when_to_use: Set execution standards simultaneously when assigning logs; used throughout stages two to three after homework starts for consolidation and follow-up.
335.trigger: When mood fluctuations, low spirits, or anxiety occur; when emotional fluctuations, behavioral adjustments, or new thoughts occur daily; when progress needs to be reported in the session or execution needs to be prompted.

221.skill_name: Review Log Homework and Provide Feedback
221.skill_description: In subsequent sessions, ask the visitor to share the records and completion status, select segments for discussion and clarification, assess their ability to identify and evaluate automatic thoughts, correct omissions and normalize difficulties, provide affirmation and encouragement, adjust subsequent intervention focus and homework arrangements accordingly, consolidating self-monitoring habits.
221.when_to_use: At the start or guidance phase of each follow-up session, used to review homework and consolidate monitoring habits.
221.trigger: When the visitor brings in homework progress or verbal report, encounters difficulties with recording, or completion status is unclear and needs verification.

289.skill_name: Arranging continuous recording and promoting transfer
289.skill_description: Arrange weekly homework, continuously record thoughts, emotions, and evidence in important situations, apply learned methods to different life scenarios, compare changes in emotional ratings and reactions, track behavioral experiments and cognitive restructuring; adjust homework based on completion and status during follow-up to enhance persistence and effectiveness.
289.when_to_use: From establishing a relationship until the entire counseling process, emphasizing the stages of transfer and continuous monitoring after homework analysis and strategy formulation.
289.trigger: When the client forms new cognitions or coping strategies in sessions, experiences emotional fluctuations, or faces real-life distress, requiring consolidation in daily practice and recording.

288.skill_name: Teaching and demonstrating thought record sheets
288.skill_description: Provide psychoeducation, explain the link between situation—automatic thought—emotion, demonstrate and lead practice in filling out thought record sheets (can start with the first three columns), record relevant evidence in specific situations, help in noticing emotions, organizing, and verifying evidence, reduce the intensity of negative emotions, and assign continuous recording between sessions.
288.when_to_use: In the stage of identifying negative automatic thoughts, or when structured organization is needed; can be used in both sessions and between sessions.
288.trigger: When the client experiences strong emotions triggered by distorted cognitions such as mind-reading, or when current emotions are intense and thoughts are chaotic and difficult to organize self-organizing.

181.skill_name: Using thought record sheets for cognitive reconstruction
181.skill_description: Fill out thought record sheets for specific triggering events, examine alternative explanations and supporting/opposing evidence, form more reasonable cognitions, and observe changes in emotional ratings to verify effectiveness; externalize the recording process outside of sessions, review, analyze, and adjust to promote cognitive reappraisal.
181.when_to_use: When conducting cognitive reconstruction training after identifying distorted automatic thoughts, or when needing continuous data outside of sessions.
181.trigger: When forming negative explanations for events and having high emotional ratings; encountering situations that trigger feelings like 'feeling dirty' or experiencing obsessive thoughts or cleaning urges.

268.skill_name: Reviewing logs to identify automatic thoughts and hypotheses
268.skill_description: Jointly review records in subsequent sessions to locate automatic thoughts and negative hypotheses in negative emotional situations, systematically review the log from the previous week and screen high-frequency and significant typical events, conduct micro-analysis of cognition—emotion—behavior, as a basis for this topic and further conceptualization.
268.when_to_use: In the second phase of psychological help (sessions 3-7) or during follow-up; in the early review and agenda-setting part of each session.
268.trigger: When the client brings back thought/emotion records or reports multiple distressing events, needing to determine the focus of the current session.

304.skill_name: Adjusting strategies based on log feedback trends
304.skill_description: Review self-monitoring records in subsequent sessions, focusing on changes in anxiety scores and trigger patterns, and provide timely feedback on progress; use representative situations as material for cognitive reappraisal or behavioral experiments, and adjust intervention strategies and homework assignments accordingly.
304.when_to_use: During review stages of each follow-up or re-examination, and when strategies need fine-tuning based on data during cognitive restructuring.
304.trigger: Log data has accumulated or scores show fluctuations; specific events (such as difficulty refusing others) appear in the record.

437.skill_description: Ask the client to recall and record the events that bothered them and the emotions at that time, and write down the potential impact on the present; or record events and internal conflicts when contradictions or indecision recur, and conduct preliminary self-analysis. Bring the log to the next session to supplement session material and track emotional changes and cognitive adjustments.
437.when_to_use: To extend assessment beyond the session, or during the interval period after a session involving trauma/emotion processing.
437.trigger: When recounting scattered or omitted, important experiences are difficult to detail in the moment; when new experiences or thoughts occur daily, or when contradictions and indecision are frequently reported.

138.skill_name: Checking and discussing emotions and meaning in the record
138.skill_description: When asking about homework completion in the next session, invite the client to share the content of the record, discuss the feelings and meaning surrounding each event, to consolidate positive experiences and promote cognitive processing and emotional regulation.
138.when_to_use: After the mood check at the beginning of each session, when reviewing homework and discussing record content.
138.trigger: When the client brings or verbalizes records such as 'three happy events daily' and seeks feedback.

375.skill_name: Encouraging and identifying difficulties based on log feedback
375.skill_description: Timely affirm progress and stability based on log feedback (such as reduced frequency), reinforce effective behaviors; at the same time, discuss difficulties encountered around the diary and practice records, offer understanding and normalization, reduce pressure, and optimize the next steps and homework.
375.when_to_use: During phase reviews or homework feedback, when positive changes are observed or obstacles need to be summarized and strategies adjusted.
375.trigger: Monitoring records show a reduction in behavior frequency (e.g., decrease in handwashing times), or the client brings/verbalizes a need to refine questions from practice records.

151.skill_name: Identify and Refine Goals by Recognizing Patterns and Triggers from Logs
151.skill_description: Lead the client to review log entries, annotate peak periods, themes, and coping tendencies (e.g., seeking external help, dependence), identify trigger patterns, and provide feedback, used for prioritizing issues, revising case conceptualization, and refining phase-oriented goals.
151.when_to_use: During each homework review and when refining conceptualization and setting phase-oriented goals.
151.trigger: Logs show recurring worries daily or before sleep, or repeated use of a single coping strategy leading to feelings of helplessness.

186.skill_name: Review Monitoring Logs and Extract Key Information
186.skill_description: Systematically review records and monitoring tables in the session, check behavioral frequency and trends, extract triggering situations, automatic thoughts, and their validity, judge whether there is improvement or maintenance, to provide basis for subsequent debate, practice, and intervention adjustments.
186.when_to_use: At the start of phase-oriented sessions or during homework review segments, when at least one week of logs has been collected.
186.trigger: Client brings or verbalizes completed records; when assessing 'no significant improvement' or emerging situations and issue entries that are discussable.

461.skill_name: Consolidate and Arrange Next Cycle Recording
461.skill_description: Briefly review the progress of the current week's records at the end of each session, provide reinforcement and encouragement, and invite the client to complete the next week's journal card to maintain monitoring habits and data continuity; adjust arrangements as necessary to enhance persistence and effectiveness.
461.when_to_use: Before the end of each session, when continuing self-monitoring arrangements and consolidating change is necessary.
461.trigger: When the completion rate of the weekly record is low or after clarification is completed, need to reiterate and schedule the next week's record.

464.skill_name: Teach and Assign Three/Five/Seven Column Thought Records
464.skill_description: Teach and assign three/five/seven column sheets, requiring recording of the situation, automatic thoughts, emotion intensity, behavioral response, supporting/opposing evidence, and alternative thoughts when experiencing emotional or physical discomfort; demonstrate filling out the five-column sheet in session and assess feasibility, for daily monitoring and between-session homework.
464.when_to_use: In the initial and subsequent stages of consultation, when introducing cognitive models and starting structured CBT processes or identifying/assessing automatic thoughts.
464.trigger: Client experiences significant negative emotions or distressing events; when preliminary understanding of 'thoughts are not facts' is achieved, requiring more structured recording.

325.skill_name: Using the Three-Column Chart to Practice Identifying and Responding to Automatic Thoughts
325.skill_description: Guide the client to systematically record specific situations, automatic thoughts, and emotional reactions on the three-column chart, and practice rational responses; compare changes in emotional intensity before and after, review scenarios and categorize, monitor daily patterns, and gradually correct dysfunctional thoughts.
325.when_to_use: When cognitive exercises and daily monitoring are needed, especially when negative automatic thoughts frequently appear in therapy or during the initial extraction of key material.
325.trigger: When automatic thoughts such as "I will be uncomfortable" or "They are ignoring me" appear in crowded or interpersonal situations, leading to anxiety or sadness, or when significant situations repeatedly occur.

167.skill_name: Guiding the Use of ABC Log and Alternatives
167.skill_description: Instruct to record using the ABC model: A for the triggering event, B for the belief, and C for the emotional/behavioral outcome, to continuously monitor daily distress; analyze the unreasonable components in B and write down alternative rational beliefs to practice, providing continuous data for subsequent argumentation and correction.
167.when_to_use: After introducing Rational Emotive Behavior Therapy/ABC theory (sessions 2-4), during the phase of daily monitoring and identifying unreasonable beliefs.
167.trigger: Intense emotional reactions and confusion about the cause; recent life events causing discomfort or confrontational behavior; when the client has understood the need to practice recording in real situations.

193.skill_name: Guiding and Collecting Key Sleep Monitoring Indicators
193.skill_description: Guide the client to use sleep records or monitoring tools to record sleep latency, number and duration of nocturnal awakenings, total sleep time, time in bed, wake-up time, and sleep efficiency, and standardize the recording items and periods (e.g., continuous for ≥7 days); supplement with information such as daytime lying in bed and fatigue when necessary, for assessment and tracking.
193.when_to_use: Throughout the assessment and intervention for insomnia-related issues, especially for establishing a baseline and early tracking after the first consultation.
193.trigger: When the client reports poor sleep and is willing to record, or when continuous, objective sleep data is needed to support diagnosis and plan; when bringing monitoring data for discussion.

520.skill_name: Using a Sleep Diary to Assess Efficacy and Provide Adjustments
520.skill_description: Conduct phased assessments based on changes in sleep efficiency, number of awakenings, sleep latency, etc., in the continuous sleep diary; affirm progress and provide feedback; cross-check consistency with subjective daytime functioning (dreaming, daytime alertness, frequency of lying in bed and movement), and timely fine-tune intervention suggestions and homework.
520.when_to_use: During follow-up and efficacy improvement phases (sessions 2-5), and when reviewing recent sleep and daytime status during each follow-up.
520.trigger: When the diary shows improvement or worsening trends in various indicators; when monitoring indicators show changes or abnormalities, or when the client reports increased dreaming, daytime fatigue/not lying in bed, or changes in movement frequency.

274.skill_name: Setting up RET self-record to address unreasonable cognitions
274.skill_description: Set up a weekly RET self-record, requiring recording the triggering event and corresponding unreasonable cognition when negative emotions arise, then writing out B based on A and C, and attempting to write out an alternative reasonable cognition, as a basis for discussion and identification of the relationship between cognitions and emotions, to be continuously used for daily application and consolidation.
274.when_to_use: Set up during the initial assessment phase, and continue to use in subsequent sessions after explaining the ABC theory.
274.trigger: Experiencing negative emotions within a week; understanding the ABC model but still attributing anxiety to the event itself or difficulty resolving conflicts.

418.skill_name: Checking and discussing the RET self-record to correct beliefs
418.skill_description: In the next session, check the completion status of the RET self-record, jointly analyze the recorded erroneous cognitions and maladaptive habits, engage in rational refutation, and grasp current changes; encourage transferring the method to other life events to consolidate cognitive change.
418.when_to_use: When reviewing or assessing the current situation at the start of subsequent sessions, particularly applicable in the second to fourth consultation stages.
418.trigger: Client brings back the completed RET self-record or raises confusion and difficulties with the record; realizing the unreasonable cognition but emotions are recurrent and conflicts are hard to resolve.

384.skill_name: Gathering primary parenting background and caregiving structure
384.skill_description: Inquire and record who raised the client in childhood, parents' occupations and family economic situation, family atmosphere, and quality of parental relationships, while forming an overall impression of the caregivers and the tone of interaction, as foundational data for understanding early emotional experiences and sources of security.
384.when_to_use: When collecting longitudinal background data or before conceptualization, when early upbringing and family information are needed.
384.trigger: Client mentions clues such as family, parents, childhood experiences, separation from parents, family structure, and economic situation.

516.skill_name: Exploring parenting styles, emotional responses, and key events
516.skill_description: Guide the narrative of parental demands and disciplinary methods, communication and emotional responses (such as hitting, denial, or lack of support), and high expectations and rules, follow up with impression events related to the caregiver and feelings at that time, clarifying clues about the long-term impact of these on current cognitions, emotions, and relationship patterns.
516.when_to_use: During the longitudinal conceptualization and exploration of early experiences, when understanding the source of core beliefs and emotional experiences is necessary.
516.trigger: Client talks about being hit, lack of care, high parental expectations, poor communication, or family conflicts during childhood memories.

228.skill_name: Reviewing Parenting Experiences and Family/Care Arrangements
228.skill_description: Guide the recall of early life experiences such as parental divorce, living with grandparents, who provided long-term care and living arrangements, record impressions and emotional reactions to the caregivers, providing a background for parenting and attachment for longitudinal conceptualization.
228.when_to_use: During the assessment of family background and the longitudinal conceptualization phase, when reviewing early parenting and care information.
228.trigger: When the client talks about the family of origin, grandparental care, parental divorce, or experiences of being cared for by relatives.

525.skill_name: Inquiring About Parental Demands, Evaluations, and Their Impact
525.skill_description: Specifically inquire about parental demands and criticisms, core expectations, and caregiving styles, record the degree of compliance and the resulting self-evaluations and concern for others' opinions, providing basis for subsequent belief and schema analysis.
525.when_to_use: During longitudinal information gathering and review of early experiences, when identifying the impact of parental expectations and evaluation patterns on the present.
525.trigger: When the client talks about strict parental demands, being criticized or worried about disappointing others, or being concerned about evaluations.

146.skill_name: Inquiring About Caregiver Response Patterns and Parenting Styles
146.skill_description: Interview the client or parent about the caregiver's response to rules and demands, level of companionship and involvement, frequency of communication, and emotional support, characterize the impact of parenting style on the client's behavior and emotions, providing input for conceptualization.
146.when_to_use: During the assessment of family background and early parenting styles or longitudinal data collection phases.
146.trigger: When clues of indulgence, neglect, strict discipline, or insufficient support appear, needing to clarify family interaction patterns.

255.skill_name: Mapping Parental Relationship Conflicts and Key Family Events
255.skill_description: Understand the quality of the parental relationship and conflict situations, follow up on key events such as multiple affairs or frequent arguments and their impact on parenting investment and the client's feelings, as important clues for the early upbringing environment.
255.when_to_use: During the detailed description of parenting history and the input phase of longitudinal conceptualization, when identifying key family events.
255.trigger: When the client talks about poor parental relationships, conflicts, or clues about the impact of early interactions on the present.

214.skill_name: Inquiring about parental parenting style and guidance support
214.skill_description: Specifically inquire about parental expectations and demands, the extent of guidance and support in academics and life, and parenting characteristics (such as indulgence, authoritarianism, or democratic), record points like "lack of correct guidance," and assess their impact on self-control and frustration tolerance.
214.when_to_use: In the initial assessment and longitudinal conceptualization phase, when identifying the role of family parenting factors.
214.trigger: When the client mentions low parental involvement, poor frustration coping ability, insufficient family support, or high expectations.

233.skill_name: Exploring the impact of comparison, punishment, and family atmosphere
233.skill_description: Detail the family atmosphere and discipline strategies such as neglectful/authoritarian parenting, overprotection, comparison and devaluation by others, intimidation, or violence, clarifying their long-term impact on inferiority and rule formation.
233.when_to_use: In the exploration of family parenting styles and longitudinal conceptualization phase, when grasping parenting characteristics and their influence.
233.trigger: When the client talks about being compared, devalued, intimidated, beaten, or parents living separately due to assertiveness.

434.skill_name: Guiding the narration of early care structure and caregiver characteristics
434.skill_description: Encourage narration of nanny/grandparent care, composition and changes of primary caregivers, caregiver personality and expression style, and caregiving methods, capturing key details to understand the role of early interactions and attachment background on current problems.
434.when_to_use: When conducting longitudinal conceptualization and collecting background information on upbringing.
434.trigger: When talking about childhood care, caregiver personality, or changes in family members and care arrangements.

331.skill_name: Follow-up questioning about key events and reactions related to caregivers
331.skill_description: Detail the situation and caregiver reactions (such as lack of support or belief in others) around memorable events, record the emotions and meaning at that time, identify emotional neglect and attachment experiences, to provide a basis for understanding current distress.
331.when_to_use: When identifying the quality of the caregiver's response and support in early life events.
331.trigger: When the client mentions being insulted, unsupported, compared, or having strong emotional memories but lacking detail.

474.skill_name: Recording Conflict Events and Impact on Caregivers
474.skill_description: Review high-conflict or extreme interaction events with caregivers and subjective experiences (such as frequent arguments, belittling), annotate emotions and meanings, and assess their impact on current beliefs, sense of security, and relationship patterns.
474.when_to_use: When exploring how early parent-child interactions affect current problems and relationship patterns.
474.trigger: When the client describes being criticized, denied, misunderstood, family conflict, or experiencing violence.

495.skill_name: Collecting Background and Caregiver Characteristics Impressions
495.skill_description: Record family structure and resources, singleton status and caregiving methods, social and communication characteristics of primary caregivers, and the client's impressions of them, extract clues related to self-care and social skills to understand current problems.
495.when_to_use: In the causal analysis and longitudinal conceptualization phase, when supplementing the background.
495.trigger: When discussing family situations, sources of personality, client's difficulties with self-care/social interaction, or evaluations of caregiver traits.

300.skill_name: Reviewing Growth and Parenting Experiences and Parental Expectations
300.skill_description: Encourage reviewing specific experiences such as upbringing conditions, strict requirements/reward mechanisms, and parents' expectations for academics, record feelings at that time, and make an initialsorting/organization of early family relationships and their impact.
300.when_to_use: In the initial consultation or growth history collection phase, to understand family education and expectations.
300.trigger: When the client mentions interactions with family, being asked/neglected, or starting to narrate details of family education.

481.skill_name: Connecting Current Interaction Patterns with Early Parenting
481.skill_description: Use comparative questions (e.g., "Is this like the demands from your parents when you were little?") to help link current ways of interacting with early upbringing, and follow up on their ongoing impact on current emotions and personality traits.
481.when_to_use: When current interactions are suspected to be influenced by early upbringing, and connection and awareness need to be established.
481.trigger: When cognitive/behavioral patterns similar to early family discipline appear in the session, or when the client proactively establishes a connection.

534.skill_name: Reviewing family atmosphere, parental relationships, and companionship
534.skill_description: Guide recollection of early family atmosphere, parental relationships and conflicts, frequency and manner of parental companionship, record the experience at that time, and understand its impact on sense of security and emotional reactions.
534.when_to_use: During longitudinal conceptualization of early parenting exploration or discussions about family background.
534.trigger: When the client mentions family discord or violence, father being absent for long periods, etc., experiences with strong emotions.

452.skill_name: Collecting parental parenting styles, expectations, and early roles
452.skill_description: Record parental parenting styles and expectations (e.g., "Study hard and you will succeed") and early family roles and responsibilities (doing chores, taking care of younger siblings), understand their impact on self-expectations and interaction patterns.
452.when_to_use: During the phase of inquiring about growth and family background, when needing to supplement role and expectation information.
452.trigger: When the client talks about parents' work, expectations for learning, or experiences of doing chores/caring for younger siblings in childhood.

156.skill_name: Inquiring about key interactions and emotions of caregivers
156.skill_description: Guide recollection of representative interaction snippets and exact quotes with caregivers, collect high-impact events such as being blamed, punished, or in conflict and the emotions at that time, and record the caregiver's emotional expression and the family emotional atmosphere, to understand the source of beliefs.
156.when_to_use: During the phase of inquiring about the details of parent-child relationships and emotional reactions, when obtaining key snippets.
156.trigger: When talking about intense emotional memories with parents, negative interactions, or noticeable emotional changes (looking down, unnatural expression).

247.skill_name: Mapping family structure and guardianship/care changes
247.skill_description: Ask along a timeline about parental marriage and guardianship changes, primary caregivers, and living arrangements, clarify the early nurturing environment and attachment trajectory, providing structural background for subsequent conceptualization.
247.when_to_use: During the initial stage of collecting early parenting history or establishing a timeline of family events.
247.trigger: When the client narrates about parental arguments/divorce, who they lived with, or changes in caregivers.

155.skill_name: Inquire about early separation, caregiving, and sources of security
155.skill_description: Inquire about experiences of separation from parents, care by ancestors, and closeness with parents, to understand the potential impact of early caregiving patterns and sources of security on current issues.
155.when_to_use: Phase of collecting longitudinal development history and early parenting information.
155.trigger: When the client mentions experiences of separation from parents in childhood, being raised by others, or parent-child estrangement.

161.skill_name: Review key decisions made based on parental opinions
161.skill_description: Record key decisions made based on parental opinions, such as academic choices, along with the feelings and meaning at the time, as material to grasp key nodes of parenting influence, connecting to current beliefs and stress experiences.
161.when_to_use: When exploring the influence of caregivers and the formation of core beliefs.
161.trigger: When the client narrates events such as important academic choices made based on parental opinions.

262.skill_name: Inquire about parental comparison and evaluation styles and their influence
262.skill_description: Understand if the client is often compared or emphasized for shortcomings, record the resulting self-evaluations such as 'incompetence' or 'inferiority,' and stress experiences, and connect with clues about the impact of strict demands and parenting styles on personality and self-demands.
262.when_to_use: Phase of discussing parenting styles and the source of self-concept.
262.trigger: When the client talks about being compared, criticized, or subjected to high expectations, and clues about personality formation.

503.skill_name: Inquire about primary caregiver and companionship patterns
503.skill_description: Ask who raised the client, the frequency and division of parental companionship, who lived with whom from childhood, and the quality of the relationship, to understand the early foundation of emotional supply and attachment experiences.
503.when_to_use: Beginning of probing longitudinal development history and parenting experiences or in assessment interviews.
503.trigger: When the client mentions caregiving styles, single-parent upbringing, or experiences of parents being frequently separated.

403.skill_name: Assessment of Parent-Child Relationship Quality and Expectations
403.skill_description: Understanding the impression and emotional experience with parents (such as closeness or distance), communication status, and expectations placed upon the individual, and identifying the influence of the resulting sense of responsibility and self-set on the present.
403.when_to_use: When transforming parenting history into relationship quality and belief cues.
403.trigger: When the client mentions cues about parental expectations, closeness/distance, or lack of communication and emotional support.

350.skill_name: Inquiring about Parental Expectations, Strictness, and Punishment Experiences
350.skill_description: Exploring details surrounding the level of expectations, strictness of demands, supervision of learning, and blame/corporal punishment, assessing their long-term impact on self-worth and emotional regulation, as a key input for conceptualization.
350.when_to_use: When needing to understand the impact of parenting style on current issues or during early parenting review.
350.trigger: When the client mentions emotional reactions related to learning pressure, being strictly required, being punished, or emotional reactions to demands from family.

207.skill_name: Connecting Parenting Experiences with Personality Coping Patterns
207.skill_description: Guiding the connection between early experiences and current traits (introversion, sensitivity, poor frustration tolerance, external attribution, low sense of control, etc.), recording subjective experiences and explanatory cues, for the longitudinal conceptualization of impact chains.
207.when_to_use: To collect impact chains or identify early-present connections before longitudinal conceptualization.
207.trigger: When the client mentions personality traits or associations between the problem and early experiences.

445.skill_name: Collecting Significant and Impressionistic Events Related to Caregivers
445.skill_description: Recording specific ages and key family events (such as the death of a relative, remarriage, etc.) and direct quotes and contexts of interactions with caregivers (being scolded, being taken away, being burned and scolded, etc.), as material for examining the caregiving relationship and belief formation.
445.when_to_use: When reviewing important nodes in caregiver interactions or needing to understand the meaning of events.
445.trigger: When the client provides specific time points, intense emotional memories, or expresses feelings of being ignored, unloved, or unexpecting.

477.skill_name: Inquire about family communication, parenting styles, and negative events
477.skill_description: Follow up on whether communication was proactive, if parenting was strict, detail experiences of being criticized, physically punished, or beaten without a clear reason, record emotions and meaning at the time, and extract their potential impact on personality and current issues.
477.when_to_use: During longitudinal conceptualization and background information gathering, when exploring the source of unreasonable beliefs.
477.trigger: When the client mentions parents being strict, little communication, being beaten/humiliated, or not achieving ideal grades.

201.skill_name: Assess parenting style and family power structure
201.skill_description: Describe the father's domineering authoritarian, absolute authority, and critical suppression style, the mother's gentle nature but lack of verbal authority, and the family's attitude towards emotional expression, assess the impact on traits such as inferiority and compliance and the formation of rules.
201.when_to_use: During longitudinal data collection and core belief clue exploration.
201.trigger: When the client complains about suppression, expresses vulnerability, punishment, or being considered 'shamed'.

154.skill_name: Clarify caregiver, parental marriage, and contact patterns
154.skill_description: Confirm parental marital status, primary caregiver, and frequency and quality of contact with parents, sort out early caregiving structure and separation history, clarify attachment lines and sources of support.
154.when_to_use: Before longitudinal conceptualization, to clarify the early nurturing environment and attachment lines.
154.trigger: When the client mentions family changes, long-term separation from parents, or the situation of the primary caregiver.

532.skill_name: Inquire about early separation, foster care, and communication patterns
532.skill_description: Specifically understand early foster care/boarding, absence due to parents being busy, communication methods, and willingness to talk, clarify early attachment and self-soothing patterns and their current impact, and trace changes in care during infancy.
532.when_to_use: When signs of abnormal early care arrangements or long-term emotional neglect appear.
532.trigger: When the client narrates experiences such as long-term care by ancestors, little communication, or changes in care during infancy.

372.skill_name: Sorting through parental relationship changes and major family events
372.skill_description: Establish a timeline around major events such as parental marital discord, divorce/remarriage, recalling experiences and meanings at the time, presenting the impact of relationship evolution on emotions and adaptation, serving as a basis for longitudinal conceptualization.
372.when_to_use: Assessment of the impact of the family of origin and parent-child relationship, longitudinal conceptualization phase.
372.trigger: When the client mentions divorce/remarriage, living with a stepfamily, or hidden family events.

442.skill_name: Investigate foster care experience, separate and its influence
442.skill_description: Clarify the time and individuals of foster care, caregiver changes, and boarding experiences, and record communication quality and emotions at the time, assessing their impact on attachment and emotional development, connecting to personality and social changes.
442.when_to_use: In-depth inquiry of specific events in upbringing history or in discussions about family trees.
442.trigger: When the client mentions being fostered, parents leaving, boarding school, or clues about personality/social changes.

349.skill_name: Organize primary caregivers, parenting styles, and expectations
349.skill_description: Outline the primary caregivers and parenting styles (e.g., little time together/frequent separation, raised by mother, emphasis on academic achievement, strict expectations) and the client's impressions, as background clues for belief formation in longitudinal conceptualization.
349.when_to_use: Collection of developmental history and family background inquiry before longitudinal conceptualization.
349.trigger: When the client mentions who primarily raised them, parental parenting styles, and expectations for academic performance.

391.skill_name: Interviewing early upbringing, relationships, and key event influences
391.skill_description: In-depth interview about experiences of growing up with grandparents, parental divorce, and emotional neglect on inferiority sensitivity and interpersonal trust, and supplementing information about the growth environment, material conditions, and communication quality to support conceptualization.
391.when_to_use: Inquiry about early upbringing and family of origin stages, for collecting material for longitudinal conceptualization.
391.trigger: When the client begins to talk about the family of origin, the nurtured individual, childhood experiences, family resources, and communication quality.

302.skill_name: Formulate and document diagnostic conclusions and basis (including scope of service and comorbidity)
302.skill_description: Provide a diagnostic conclusion based on evidence (e.g., general psychological problems/specific statements), itemize the basis (four dimensions of symptoms, course and functioning, scale scores, exclusions, etc.), confirm intact self-awareness, absence of hallucinations/delusions and major somatic abnormalities, identify and document comorbidities or traits when necessary, define consultation scope and direction of service.
302.when_to_use: After integrating information and interpreting scales, a diagnosis needs to be provided before formulating goals and plans.
302.trigger: Sufficient diagnostic clues are present and psychotic and severe problems have been ruled out; scales and clinical information are consistent, or when hospital diagnosis needs to be included in the record and explanation.

453.skill_name: Systematically assess mental status and social functioning to support differential diagnosis
453.skill_description: Systematically check and record perceptual awareness, thought, emotion, self-awareness, consistency of knowledge, and personality traits, observe consistency between clothing/demeanor and emotional expression, and assess social functioning such as learning and interpersonal relationships, determine the presence of psychotic features, and provide basis for differential diagnosis and diagnosis.
453.when_to_use: In the initial diagnosis and psychological assessment phase, used to establish a baseline of mental status and rule out psychotic manifestations.
453.trigger: Client exhibits low mood, anxiety, or functional decline, and when it is necessary to clarify the presence or absence of perceptual or thought abnormalities and the degree of social functioning impairment.

358.skill_name: Implement differential diagnosis and safety assessment
358.skill_description: Assess self-awareness, thought, and perception (hallucinations, delusions), suicide and self-harm risk, collect family and somatic/neurological history, rule out psychotic disorders and substance/somatic factors; and comprehensively assess the course features and whether reactions have generalized into preliminary statements, clarify the necessity for referral.
358.when_to_use: Before making a formal diagnosis and when atypical manifestations or symptom exacerbation occur.
358.trigger: First assessment or when risk signals such as perceptual abnormalities, suicidal ideation, drug/disease clues, poor cooperation, etc., appear.

314.skill_name: Formulate 'General Psychological Problem' diagnosis and document basis
314.skill_description: Integrate interview, assessment, and differential diagnosis results, based on the three principles of illness and health, course and functioning, scale scores, and other key indicators, clearly establish the diagnosis of 'General Psychological Problem', document traceable basis, and determine subsequent consultation goals, plans, and service settings based on this.
314.when_to_use: After completing information collection and differential diagnosis, when the final diagnosis and its basis need to be determined and documented.
314.trigger: Psychosis, neuroticism, and severe psychological problems have been ruled out, scales and clinical judgment are consistent, and the impact on social functioning is relatively mild.

313.skill_name: Assess course, generalization, and functional impairment to rule out severe problems
313.skill_description: Check if the duration is short (within about one to two months), if the reaction is limited to specific situations, and if the damage to social functioning is mild and not generalized. Use this to rule out severe psychological problems and define severity and urgency of intervention.
313.when_to_use: For severity grading and functional assessment, and in the differential stage before forming a preliminary diagnosis.
313.trigger: Although there is anxiety or decreased learning efficiency, the person can study and work normally; symptoms are limited, the course is less than two months, and social functioning is not widely impaired.

276.skill_name: Determine severe psychological problems based on symptomology
276.skill_description: Check item by item the anxiety-related symptoms and their impact on daily life, assess whether the emotional reaction has generalized and if the course exceeds two months; when multiple symptoms are evident and functional impairment is significant, and the course is long, classify as a severe psychological problem.
276.when_to_use: When determining the level and severity of the problem after ruling out psychosis.
276.trigger: Presence of multiple anxiety-related symptoms, affecting learning and daily life, with a course lasting more than two months.

465.skill_name: Mental status examination and screening for psychotic/suicidal risk
465.skill_description: Check and record during the interview for psychotic symptoms such as hallucinations or delusions, as well as suicidal ideation or behavior, clearly determine 'yes/no', and use insight and logical thinking to determine it, as a basis for risk grading and diagnostic boundaries.
465.when_to_use: For risk assessment and ruling out severe mental disorders during the diagnostic stage.
465.trigger: The client mentions abnormal perceptions, persecutory thoughts, self-harm/suicidal thoughts, or when routine severe risk screening is required.

438.skill_name: Classification judgment based on symptomology, course, and function
438.skill_description: Assess the intensity of core symptoms such as anxiety according to symptomology standards, combine with whether it is generalized, impact on social functioning, and course length, to judge as a general psychological problem and rule out severe or neurotic problems, to clarify the level of intervention.
438.when_to_use: When assessing severity and course after clarifying symptom presentation for classification judgment.
438.trigger: Symptoms are limited to specific situations, not generalized; social functioning is not severely impaired; course is about one month.

270.skill_name: Systematic assessment of mental status and social functioning to support diagnosis
270.skill_description: Based on interview observation of clothing, posture, speech clarity, self-awareness, presence of hallucinations or delusions, consistency of emotional expression, and verification of social functioning such as interpersonal and learning, to form a preliminary judgment of the nature and severity of the problem, supporting the appropriateness of working diagnosis and consultation.
270.when_to_use: Assessment and relationship building phase (1st to 2nd interview), before preliminary diagnosis.
270.trigger: Manifestations such as low mood, passive communication, or brief speech during the interview, when judging the nature and severity of symptoms is required.

218.skill_name: Integrating multiple sources of evidence to form diagnostic conclusions and severity
218.skill_description: Integrate scales, self-report/other report, and mental status observation, focusing on clues such as insomnia, poor appetite, recurrent self-harm attempts, and impaired social functioning, to form a clinical judgment of the nature and severity of the problem, clarifying the diagnosis and communicating it as a basis for subsequent plans.
218.when_to_use: After preliminary scale interpretation, when objective scores need to be verified and integrated with narratives and behaviors.
218.trigger: When scale and interview data are complete, and when anxiety/depressive levels suggesting impairment coexist, and a clear conclusion needs to be reached.

195.skill_name: Excluding neurotic problems with reality congruence and course of illness
195.skill_description: Verify whether symptoms correspond to real-life inducing events, have a shorter duration, milder functional impairment, and are not generalized, to exclude neurotic problems, and serve as an important basis for diagnostic localization.
195.when_to_use: When symptoms of anxiety or depression exist but it is necessary to distinguish whether they are neurotic problems.
195.trigger: Symptoms triggered by specific life events, lasting approximately several weeks to one month, with milder social function impact and no obvious generalization.

285.skill_name: Forming a preliminary diagnosis and itemizing the basis for documentation
285.skill_description: Synthesize information regarding the course of illness, symptoms and severity, functional impairment, and generalization, to form a preliminary diagnosis and itemize the core basis (such as triggered by real stimuli, duration, functional impact, etc.); provide specific classification and severity description when evidence supports it.
285.when_to_use: Diagnostic stage of the 1st consultation or after data collection is complete, when a preliminary diagnosis needs to be proposed and the basis explained.
285.trigger: When the client reports anxiety/insomnia lasting for several weeks or more, decreased learning efficiency, social withdrawal, or scale results indicating corresponding levels.

147.skill_name: Verify past medical diagnoses and treatment history and conduct medical screening
147.skill_description: Coordinate or exclude organic lesions based on existing consultation results, verify past hospital diagnoses and current medication status, incorporate medical information into psychological diagnosis reference, clarify consultation boundaries and service pathways.
147.when_to_use: During the assessment phase, differentiate between physical and mental factors, and clarify whether medical treatment should precede or integrate external diagnoses.
147.trigger: Chief complaint accompanied by physical discomfort or prior medical visits; client/family mentions past diagnoses and medication status.

202.skill_name: Systematically organize and record symptoms and functional impact
202.skill_description: Organize self-reported symptoms across dimensions such as emotion, cognition, behavior, and physiology, record the impact on learning and life, and combine with therapist observations (such as crying, irritability) and accompanying changes in sleep/appetite to form structured diagnostic clues.
202.when_to_use: During the psychological diagnosis phase, for the first two sessions, when needing to clarify the current symptom profile and the degree of functional impairment.
202.trigger: Client reports low mood, poor sleep, poor attention, etc., and describes the impact on classes, homework, and interpersonal relationships.

400.skill_name: Administer and interpret scales such as SAS/SDS/SCL-90 to support diagnosis
400.skill_description: Implement and interpret scales such as SAS, SDS, SCL-90, calculate standard scores and factor scores, quantify anxiety/depression and related dimensions, as objective basis for determining the nature and severity of the problem, establishing a baseline, and comparison during follow-up.
400.when_to_use: For initial diagnosis or when establishing scale baselines and diagnostic evidence; for staged assessments to compare changes.
400.trigger: Chief complaint of anxiety/depression, impact on sleep/appetite, or need to objectively quantify severity and progress.

507.skill_name: Organize course and judge generalization level and severity
507.skill_description: Clarify the duration of symptoms, whether they have generalized elsewhere, and the impact on functions such as learning and interpersonal relationships, combine short-term with limited or long-term continuous and widespread impairment to determine the level of general/severe psychological problems.
507.when_to_use: For timeline verification and course organization before forming a psychological diagnosis, or for severity grading.
507.trigger: Client can provide start time and duration, reports decreased efficiency but overall function is maintained or has been continuous for a long time and is widespread.

471.skill_name: Observe mental status and inquire about suicidal risk routinely
471.skill_description: Record mental status cues such as demeanor, eye contact, speech rate, and posture during the interview, combine with physiological manifestations of anxiety/depression, and directly inquire about suicidal ideation or plans, record the results according to standards, and assist in judging severity and safety.
471.when_to_use: At the time of diagnostic confirmation during the initial assessment and follow-up assessment, or when supplementary scales and subjective evidence are needed.
471.trigger: Appearance of low energy, reduced speech, slowed speech rate, or anxious expressions, sweating, or verbalization involving negative thoughts.

273.skill_name: Assess impairment of mental/physiological/social functioning and preliminary classification
273.skill_description: Systematically record mental/emotional manifestations such as tension and irritability, physiological states like sleep and appetite, and social function changes such as learning and social interaction, comprehensively analyze functional impairment, preliminarily classify the nature of the problem, and record aspects like insight to guide subsequent intervention.
273.when_to_use: During the initial interview assessment phase, used to determine the nature of the problem and form a preliminary diagnostic impression.
273.trigger: Client reports decreased efficiency, reduced social interaction, accompanied by obvious anxiety or physiological reactions.

448.skill_name: Rule out organic lesions and psychotic disorders
448.skill_description: Based on medical history and mental status examination, physical examination/consultation records, and family history, confirm the absence of organic lesions and psychotic symptoms, refer to hospital examinations and diagnoses when necessary for exclusion, as a basis for differential diagnosis before psychological diagnosis.
448.when_to_use: In the early stages of assessment and diagnosis, when it is necessary to first rule out organic lesions and psychotic disorders.
448.trigger: Chief complaints such as anxiety/sleep problems with no known physical cause, or when medical examinations indicate 'no organic lesions'.

414.skill_name: Rule out severe psychological problems based on functional maintenance and limitation
414.skill_description: Check if learning, interpersonal, and behavioral functions are generally maintained, if the problem is limited to a specific relationship/situation, and if the duration is less than two months; if functions are intact and not generalized, severe psychological problems are generally ruled out.
414.when_to_use: Before severity grading and referral judgment.
414.trigger: Ability to participate in school activities and normal interaction, difficulties are limited to a single situation or short-term fluctuations.

292.skill_name: Interview-based assessment and grading of suicide/self-harm risk
292.skill_description: Specifically inquire about suicidal ideation, frequency, recent occurrence, methods, and planning, combined with recent behavior and functioning, record the risk level (e.g., occasional thoughts but controllable $ightarrow$ low risk) and protective factors, to guide safety and intervention arrangements.
292.when_to_use: During depression symptom assessment and work diagnosis, or when negative thoughts and functional decline occur.
292.trigger: Client reports suicidal thoughts, feelings of hopelessness, or a history of self-harm, even if frequency is low and controllable.

321.skill_name: Initiate crisis intervention and safety management for high-risk situations
321.skill_description: After confirming the presence of suicidal ideation/intent and self-harm history or other high-risk cues, promptly initiate crisis intervention procedures, sign safety agreements if necessary, and strengthen the support network to ensure safety and gain time for subsequent treatment.
321.when_to_use: During the initial interview or assessment update, immediately manage if the assessment is determined to be medium-high risk.
321.trigger: Client describes specific self-harm/suicide plans or has engaged in dangerous behavior, frequent impulsivity and extreme distress.

318.skill_name: Identify precipitating events, primary problems, and comorbidity relationships
318.skill_description: Organize specific precipitating events (e.g., exams, breakups) and their association with symptoms, determine the primary problem (e.g., anxiety predominates) and identify comorbidities or primary/secondary relationships such as anxiety causing depression, to categorize as general psychological problems and determine intervention priority.
318.when_to_use: During the diagnostic assessment phase, when locating symptom triggers and problem hierarchies is required.
318.trigger: Reports recent significant stimuli events accompanied by anxiety/sleep disturbance and learning impairment, scales indicate prominent dominant dimension.

187.skill_name: Organize and state diagnostic basis and preliminary conclusions
187.skill_description: Integrate scales, observations, and differential conclusions into clear statements (e.g., course, functional impairment, generalization, etc.), form a preliminary diagnosis or work diagnosis, and record exclusion pathways and supporting evidence, explain to the client if necessary to enhance understanding.
187.when_to_use: After completing the scale, interview, and differential process, when diagnostic conclusions need to be provided and recorded.
187.trigger: Sufficient evidence (e.g., scales indicate mild-moderate, limited functional impairment), need to ensure diagnosis is transparent and traceable.

522.skill_name: Apply the "Three Principles" and differentiate and exclude item by item
522.skill_description: Check for congruence of objective and subjective aspects, internal coordination, and personality stability according to the "three principles" of illness and non-illness, self-awareness, and the presence of hallucinations or delusions; and combine with whether there are concrete conflicts, functional impairment, and course/generalization, to exclude psychotic disorders, neurotic disorders, and severe psychological problems item by item.
522.when_to_use: After preliminary diagnosis, to ensure diagnostic accuracy when excluding other categories of disorders.
522.trigger: No psychotic features observed, intact self-awareness; conflicts have real significance and limited social functional impairment, short course.

352.skill_name: Interpret psychological assessments and recommend medical evaluation when necessary
352.skill_description: Integrate assessment results from SCL-90, SAS, SDS, etc., with normative data to calibrate the symptom spectrum and severity (e.g., mild depression/no marked anxiety) as diagnostic corroboration; when depressive tendency and functional impairment persist, recommend further diagnosis and assessment for medication treatment needs at the hospital.
352.when_to_use: When completing psychological assessments or when objective indicators are needed to calibrate diagnosis and whether medical evaluation is required.
352.trigger: Scale scores indicate abnormality accompanied by persistent symptoms such as insomnia, or when the chief complaint and scale require cross-validation.

219.skill_name: Repeat testing and follow-up comparison to update diagnostic impression
219.skill_description: Repeat tests such as SAS/SDS during the intervention follow-up period and conduct follow-up interviews, compare changes before and after (e.g., anxiety/depression decreasing from moderate to mild), revise the diagnosis and plan accordingly, and record progress.
219.when_to_use: After the start of preliminary intervention or at stage-specific assessment points, when evaluating treatment efficacy and state evolution is required.
219.trigger: Entering the follow-up phase or the visitor reports a change in state, when previous abnormal scores need to be verified for improvement trends.

311.skill_name: Differentiate and exclude neurotic/anxious neurotic disorders
311.skill_description: Refer to the characteristics of neurotic disorders, check the degree of distress, social functional impairment, presence of avoidance and generalization, and course (e.g., whether it exceeds six months), and combine with the reality of the conflict and the score results to judge whether the neurotic disorder criteria are met; if not met, exclude it.
311.when_to_use: When there are obvious anxiety/depressive symptoms but the nature and persistence need clarification.
311.trigger: Anxiety is directly related to real events, short course, basic function is maintained, no signs of widespread avoidance or generalization.

518.skill_name: Interpreting SCL-90 Symptom Dimensions and Severity
518.skill_description: Based on the total score, positive items, and factor scores of the SCL-90, identify high-score dimensions such as interpersonal sensitivity, depression, anxiety, paranoia, etc., to define overall severity and symptom profile, assisting in the formation of quantitative basis for diagnosis and follow-up.
518.when_to_use: After completing the psychological assessment, for severity definition before diagnostic judgment.
518.trigger: When SCL-90 factor scores or total scores are significantly elevated, and abnormal dimensions and overall severity need to be determined.

226.skill_name: Administering and Interpreting Quantitative Severity of SCL-90/SAS/SDS
226.skill_description: After consent, administer SCL-90, SAS, and SDS, calculate standard scores and factor scores, determine the severity of anxiety/depression and related dimensions, and record the results as objective basis and baseline for diagnosis and treatment efficacy assessment.
226.when_to_use: For the initial assessment or when a more comprehensive understanding of emotional state and severity is needed to establish a baseline.
226.trigger: When the client reports anxiety, irritability, sleep/appetite problems, or when comparing before and after changes.

211.skill_name: Applying the 'Illness vs. Non-Illness Three Principles' to Differentiate Pathological Conditions and Rule Out Psychotic Issues
211.skill_description: Verify the unity of subjective and objective, coordination of psychological activity, and personality stability based on the three principles, assess self-awareness and the presence of hallucinations or delusions, to distinguish normal reactions from psychological disorders and rule out psychotic issues, clarifying whether it falls within the scope of psychological counseling.
211.when_to_use: In the early stages of assessment and diagnosis, to distinguish psychotic issues from general psychological problems and determine the boundary between illness and non-illness.
211.trigger: Although there are complaints such as anxiety and insomnia, logical thinking is normal, emotions and situations are commensurate, and social functioning is basically intact.

217.skill_name: Administering, Recording, and Interpreting PCL-C/SAS/SCL-90 Assessments
217.skill_description: Administer PCL-C, SAS, SCL-90, etc., completely record raw scores, factor scores, and positive items, interpret according to threshold systems, and form a preliminary diagnostic impression, serving as a basis for diagnostic judgment and severity grading.
217.when_to_use: In the middle stage of an assessment interview, when objective quantification of symptom severity is needed to provide evidence for diagnosis.
217.trigger: When there is persistent low mood, insomnia, severe anxiety, or functional impairment, and a scale quantification and diagnostic support are required.

458.skill_name: Identify concrete conflict to rule out neurotic issues
458.skill_description: Determine if psychological conflict is caused by real factors, consistent with the situation, has moral connotations, and concrete features; when emotional reactions are understandable and not broadly generalized, rule out neurotic issues, avoid over-pathologizing.
458.when_to_use: In the differential diagnosis stage, when distinguishing from neurotic issues.
458.trigger: The problem originates from real events such as work/study/intimate relationships, the range and object of the reaction are limited, and function remains basically stable.

357.skill_name: Use SCL-90 to screen symptom spectrum and comorbidity tendency
357.skill_description: Administer and interpret the total score and factor scores of the SCL-90, mark dimensions with scores $\ge 2$ (such as depression, anxiety, obsessive-compulsive, interpersonal sensitivity, etc.), identify the symptom spectrum and potential comorbidity clues, as a reference for plan formulation and follow-up comparison.
357.when_to_use: Initial diagnosis requires broad screening for other psychological symptoms or suspicion of comorbidity, and when establishing a baseline.
