357.trigger: The client reports other troubles besides the main issue, or multiple factors are elevated on the scale, requiring comprehensive assessment.

163.skill_name: Corroborate diagnosis with integrated results of SCL-90/SAS/EPQ, etc.
163.skill_description: Integrate assessment results from SCL-90, SAS/SDS, and EPQ, focusing on anxiety factors and standard scores, the severity of depression, and personality traits, calibrate consistency with clinical interview, and adjust diagnostic hypotheses and clarify key dimensions when necessary.
163.when_to_use: When objective measures are needed to assist diagnosis and grading after the interview, or when calibrating clinical judgment after completing assessments.
163.trigger: Scale results are available and indicate elevated relevant dimensions or personality tendencies, requiring cross-validation with the chief complaint.

478.skill_name: Rule out severe mental illness by combining 'Three Principles' with self-awareness
478.skill_description: Based on the three principles of normal and abnormal mental activity, combined with self-awareness, active help-seeking, and the absence of hallucinations or disorganized thinking, record the reasons for ruling out severe mental illness, complete key differential diagnosis, and direct subsequent diagnosis.
478.when_to_use: In the early screening and diagnostic stage to determine the existence of severe mental illness.
478.trigger: The client is aware of the abnormality and actively seeks help, has good real-world contact, and shows no symptoms of mental illness.

435.skill_name: Explain and provide feedback on scale results to the client and family
435.skill_description: Use explanation techniques to provide the client and their father with the meaning of SDS/SAS scores, clarify the current state and risk, enhance consistent understanding of the issue, promote motivation for cooperation and subsequent intervention, and link to subsequent plans.
435.when_to_use: During the feedback phase in the initial diagnosis or assessment stage after the scale administration is complete and results are obtained.
435.trigger: Test results show mild depression or moderate anxiety, and the client and family have doubts about the meaning of the scores and subsequent plans or need to unify understanding.

317.skill_name: Interpret and record scale results to determine severity and characteristics
317.skill_description: Organize and interpret the test results, such as judging anxiety levels based on SAS, identifying significant symptom domains based on SCL-90 factors and total score, determining personality tendencies based on EPQ, and recording the conclusions in the assessment and diagnosis to provide a basis for subsequent goals and plans.
317.when_to_use: When writing the assessment and diagnosis or discussing results with the client after the test has been completed and scores are obtained.
317.trigger: Test report generated and includes key scores, factors, and personality dimension information.

436.skill_name: Re-test SAS/SDS and compare pre-post consultation effectiveness
436.skill_description: Have the client complete the anxiety and depression self-report scales again before consolidation and termination, compare the changes in scores before and after, to objectively evaluate the consultation effectiveness and use it as a basis for a stage assessment or termination; record standard score changes for effect evaluation and plan adjustment.
436.when_to_use: In the later stages of consultation or at the end of assessment and stage summaries, when the therapeutic effect needs to be quantitatively re-verified.
436.trigger: Signs of symptom improvement exist or objective verification and recording of intervention effect are needed, preparing for a stage evaluation or termination of consultation.

432.skill_name: Initial assessment: Administer SAS/SDS to establish baseline for anxiety and depression
432.skill_description: Administer SAS and SDS in the first assessment to quantify anxiety and depression levels, obtain standard scores and clinical classifications, serve as a baseline for diagnosis and subsequent re-testing comparison, and supplement interview materials.
432.when_to_use: During the psychological assessment and diagnosis stage (first consultation), when objectively quantifying anxiety and depression symptoms is required.
432.trigger: The client reports emotional distress such as sadness, restlessness, anxiety, poor sleep, decreased learning efficiency, etc., requiring severity assessment.

283.skill_name: Initial assessment using SAS/SDS/SCL-90 and symptom quantification
283.skill_description: Administer SAS, SDS, and SCL-90 in the initial assessment phase to obtain standard scores and factor scores, objectively quantify symptoms such as anxiety, and provide a basis for preliminary diagnosis and severity judgment.
283.when_to_use: In the diagnostic phase of the first consultation, when objective quantification of symptoms such as anxiety and insomnia is needed for preliminary diagnosis.
283.trigger: Client reports anxiety, palpitations, insomnia, etc.; when verbal reports are insufficient to determine severity or objective information is required.

351.skill_name: Compare pre- and post-test scores and evaluate counseling effectiveness
351.skill_description: Repeat administration of SCL-90, SAS, and SDS before and after counseling, compare score changes, and calculate score reduction rates, combined with social functioning improvement, to quantitatively evaluate intervention effectiveness and treatment efficacy.
351.when_to_use: In the evaluation/termination phase or when summarizing treatment effects and needing to decide on a course of action.
351.trigger: Completion of a treatment cycle, when quantitative treatment effect is needed or a decision on adjusting the plan is required.

162.skill_name: Analyze and provide feedback on test results to formulate the counseling plan
162.skill_description: Combine SCL-90, SAS, EPQ scores with the client's statements to explain and provide feedback on the test results, clarify the nature and severity of the problem based on the test results, and subsequently determine the counseling method and subsequent goals.
162.when_to_use: In the step where test results are reported back and the counseling plan is formulated after the initial assessment testing.
162.trigger: Test scoring is complete and it is necessary to inform the client of the assessment findings and clarify the subsequent counseling method and plan.

316.skill_name: Select and administer targeted scales after obtaining consent
316.skill_description: Based on the client's problem characteristics, after obtaining their consent, select targeted scales (such as SAS, SCL-90, EPQ) to administer to obtain standardized data, supplement consultation materials, and provide a basis for judgment of severity and personality traits.
316.when_to_use: In the initial assessment or evaluation phase when objective quantification is needed to support judgment and goal setting.
316.trigger: Client presents complaints such as anxiety, sleep disorders, interpersonal difficulties, and agrees to undergo psychological testing.

296.skill_name: Measure and Interpret SAS to Determine Anxiety Severity
296.skill_description: Use the Anxiety Self-Rating Scale (SAS) for standardized assessment, calculate and interpret standard scores, quantify current anxiety levels, assist in determining the presence or absence of anxiety symptoms, and cross-reference with interview information, serving as a reference for subsequent interventions.
296.when_to_use: When quantifying mental state during the initial interview, or when the client reports anxiety-related symptoms such as mood fluctuations, insomnia, or worry.
296.trigger: Client reports significant mood fluctuations, long-term insomnia, worry about the future; need to objectify the anxiety level.

303.skill_name: Integrate Assessment and Symptom Data to Formulate Diagnostic Tendency
303.skill_description: Comprehensively analyze SAS, SDS scores with the client's symptom descriptions, impairment in social functioning, and other data to judge the tendency for obsessive tendencies and accompanying anxiety or depression severity, form a preliminary diagnosis and problem statement, and incorporate test results into the diagnostic basis.
303.when_to_use: When making assessment and diagnostic conclusions after the initial interview and scale assessment are complete.
303.trigger: SAS/SDS results obtained, and key information such as symptom duration and functional impact is known.

450.skill_name: Periodic Re-testing of SDS/SAS to Monitor Changes and Efficacy of Treatment
450.skill_description: Administer SDS and SAS at key points during counseling (such as early and ninth sessions), compare pre- and post-scores to evaluate mood changes and treatment effects, providing a basis for plan adjustment and termination.
450.when_to_use: Before and after the middle and consolidation phases of formal counseling, or when re-testing is needed to monitor progress.
450.trigger: Need to evaluate treatment efficacy or consider phase transition/termination; client's state shows significant improvement or persistent distress.

134.skill_name: Interpret SDS/SAS Scores to Determine Severity and Formulate Conclusions
134.skill_description: Based on SDS and SAS scores and cut-off ranges, determine the level of depression/anxiety (e.g., mild, moderate, severe), form concise conclusions for assessment, communication, and record-keeping, supporting subsequent decisions.
134.when_to_use: Used during case assessment summary and preliminary diagnosis stages after the scale scores are available.
134.trigger: SDS or SAS scores indicate a medium to high level, requiring clarification of the nature and severity of the problem.

234.skill_name: Recommend medical consultation for diagnosis based on scale results
234.skill_description: When scale results indicate moderate anxiety or moderate to severe depression, clearly inform the client of the test results and recommend seeking further diagnosis and assessment at a professional medical institution as soon as possible to obtain standardized treatment recommendations.
234.when_to_use: When the test score reaches the relevant diagnostic threshold or indicates moderate to severe problems, and medical diagnosis and treatment recommendations are needed.
234.trigger: SAS standard score around 63 indicates moderate anxiety; SDS index around 0.62 indicates moderate to severe depression.

332.skill_name: Periodic re-testing and comparison of scores before and after to evaluate intervention effect
332.skill_description: Re-test the same scale at the end of an intervention or at a stage point, compare the score changes before and after to evaluate the effect and the degree of symptom improvement, using data to verify goal achievement.
332.when_to_use: When consulting enters the consolidation or summary phase, and the effect of the intervention needs to be evaluated.
332.trigger: Completion of a predetermined number of interventions or need to verify goal achievement and symptom changes.

242.skill_name: Re-test the same scale and compare to evaluate treatment effect changes
242.skill_description: At the effect evaluation stage, re-test the same scale and compare the changes in standard scores to determine if anxiety, etc., have alleviated, quantify the effect of the intervention and the trend of change, used for interim summaries or ending decisions.
242.when_to_use: For interim summaries or ending consultations, used to evaluate treatment effect and trends of change.
242.trigger: Need to objectively verify symptom changes and treatment effect after the intervention has been implemented for a period of time.

524.skill_name: Administer SAS to assess anxiety level and determine anxiety severity
524.skill_description: Use the SAS scale to assess the intensity of the client's anxiety, calculate the total score, and determine the severity according to the scale standards (e.g., moderate), forming a quantitative conclusion, as a baseline reference for anxiety problem judgment and intervention.
524.when_to_use: For initial diagnosis or before intervention, when anxiety level needs to be quantified and severity determined.
524.trigger: Client's main complaints are fear, tension, and unease, and the anxiety level needs to be clarified.

533.skill_name: Administer SDS to quantify depression severity and interpret results
533.skill_description: Use SDS in the initial interview to quantitatively assess the level of depression, record raw scores and standard scores, interpret according to norms, clarify current depression severity, supplement interview information, and provide a basis for subsequent goals and plans.
533.when_to_use: Initial diagnosis or assessment phase, when objective understanding of depression level and supplementation of interview information is needed.
533.trigger: Client reports persistent low mood, insomnia, irritability, desire to drop out, and other depression-related symptoms.

150.skill_name: Administer and interpret SCL-90 to quantify multidimensional symptom profile
150.skill_description: Administer and interpret the total score, number of positive items, and scores for each factor of the SCL-90. Identify prominent dimensions such as anxiety, depression, interpersonal sensitivity, hostility, etc., based on norms, quantify the range and severity of symptoms, and provide objective basis for assessment and conceptualization.
150.when_to_use: Initial assessment phase, when objective understanding of the symptom profile and breadth of distress is needed, and to provide a baseline for conceptualization and goal setting.
150.trigger: Client reports various discomforts such as anxiety, restlessness, sleep problems, and verbal information is insufficient to define severity or range.

278.skill_name: Compare quantitative presentation of treatment effect and change before and after measurement
278.skill_description: Repeat the same scale in the later stages of counseling to compare changes in scores before and after (e.g., addiction, social avoidance, sleep, AAQ-II), test the effectiveness of the intervention, summarize the effects, and support case closure assessment.
278.when_to_use: When counseling enters the summary or staged assessment phase, used to verify the extent of improvement and achievement of goals.
278.trigger: Objective verification of change after multiple interventions or to provide evidence of counseling effectiveness.

267.skill_name: Administer SCL-90 and complete informed consent to establish baseline
267.skill_description: In the initial interview assessment phase, explain and complete informed consent, guide the completion of the record form including the SCL-90, obtain quantitative baseline data for symptoms such as depression and anxiety, to provide a basis for subsequent assessment and plan development.
267.when_to_use: First stage assessment and relationship building phase (1st to 2nd session), when establishing a quantitative baseline is required.
267.trigger: Start of the initial consultation, when a systematic understanding of the client's symptom status or abnormality is indicated, leading to assessment.

272.skill_name: Monitor Efficacy by Comparing SCL-90 Before and After
272.skill_description: Administer the SCL-90 assessment before and after the intervention to compare changes in factors such as somatization, depression, and anxiety, to objectively evaluate symptom improvement and reduction in subjective distress, providing evidence for efficacy judgment.
272.when_to_use: During phase reviews or at the end of a phase, when evaluating the effect of the intervention.
272.trigger: When treatment reaches a predetermined point (such as the end of a phase or case closure), or when the client reports symptom changes requiring objective verification.

440.skill_name: Re-test SCL-90 and Assess Effect by Comparison
440.skill_description: Re-test the SCL-90 (and TAS) after the intervention or before case closure, compare with the initial assessment, and observe whether factor scores return to the normal range, to assess the relief of anxiety and consulting effectiveness.
440.when_to_use: During phase assessments or before ending consultation, when needing to verify the timing of intervention effect and symptom improvement.
440.trigger: When the client reports reduced anxiety, ability to concentrate on learning, and improved social interaction, requiring quantitative data to confirm subjective improvement.

483.skill_name: Re-measure at Follow-up Stage to Monitor Maintenance Effect
483.skill_description: Re-administer a standardized scale consistent with the baseline (such as SDS, LSAS, AIS/SAS) at the end of consultation or at follow-up points, compare scores and level changes, to evaluate the maintenance of efficacy and symptom changes, as a basis for follow-up and subsequent recommendations.
483.when_to_use: At the end of the consultation phase or during follow-up assessments, when needing to objectively quantify efficacy changes or maintenance status.
483.trigger: At the end of a two-week or three-month follow-up, requiring quantitative verification of subjective improvement or reporting symptom fluctuations.

504.skill_name: Administer and Interpret EPQ to Identify Personality Tendencies
504.skill_description: Administer the EPQ and report scores for the E, N, P, and L dimensions, to identify personality backgrounds such as extraversion-introversion, emotional instability, and masking tendencies, to assist in case conceptualization and plan selection.
504.when_to_use: Initial assessment to understand the impact of personality traits on the problem, to support case conceptualization and risk identification.
504.trigger: When the client exhibits characteristics such as sensitivity, impulsivity, or hostility in interpersonal and emotional reactions, and personality tendencies are unclear.
